messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a tail of OOMs and 2–3x latency spikes on pool-eu-west yesterday. GPU util on node-gpu-7 was ~98% for ~3h, a bunch of short-lived jobs kept blocking KV cache eviction. Anyone else seeing noisy neighbor behavior?

kevin: Saw that. Router logs show we started routing some inference traffic into the dedicated pool after fallback rules triggered. Might be an affinity/routing mismatch; past midnight spike correlated with recurring batch jobs. Paste of recent router decision: ```{
  route: inference-eu
  selected_pool: dedicated-eu-1 (fallback)
  reason: capacity_overflow(hosted-eu)
  flags: prefer_low_latency=false, preemptible=false
}```

sofia: Is this related to the soft-quota rollout? We set eviction at 0.85 but a few workloads are pinning the GPU memory and preventing KV cache reclaim. Also saw unusually high NVLink TX during that window.

dinesh: Two angles: 1) enforce GPU affinity + preemption windows (so burst jobs get labeled preemptible), 2) use taints/tolerations + guaranteed QoS for Dedicated customers. We can also experiment with MIG partitions for noisy tenants.

maria: Agree on affinity + preemption. Hard taints help isolation but kill packing efficiency — cost tradeoff. What about a hybrid: reserve a fractional slice of GPUs per node for dedicated traffic and route to them only when needed? That keeps utilization higher most of the time but isolates during tails.

kevin: Could do a router flag + label approach: mark burst/pipeline jobs with `redwood/preemptible=true` and make router prefer preemptible quota when under pressure. Simple change in routing policy and a canary rollout.

infra-bot: alert: node-gpu-7 memory_pressure=true (1745027003) :warning:

sofia: Also calling out networking: the P2P memcpy between pods sharing the same PCI bus was saturating NVLink and causing per-token latency to spike. MIG partitioning or colocating high-bandwidth pods could help.

dinesh: Cost note — reserving ~20% of GPUs as dedicated across nodes increases unit cost ~12% in our sim, but reduces SLA tail misses by >90% in the worst-case workload. Need product signoff for any persistent reservation.

maria: Proposed plan: Kevin prototypes router change + preemptible label in canary (eu-west-1). Dinesh to draft taint/toleration + eviction policy (soft window + hard cutoff). Sofia to run MIG/packing bench on node-gpu-7 equivalents and share perf deltas. Target: canary next Tue, monitor 72h. :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll open a PR for router rules and add unit/integration tests. Will link the PR here once ready.

maria: Thanks — if anyone objects or has alternative suggestions drop them in this thread. Also: add dashboard panels for per-node NVLink TX/RX and preemption counts so we can track regressions.

kevin: noted, will add dashboard cards under eng-infra -> gpu-telemetry.

sofia: adding MIG config matrix to the ticket.

maria: closing loop — assign owners in the ticket later today.
